title: Traverse a synchronized list under its own lock

blocks.text: `Collections.synchronizedList` makes each call on the list synchronized, but its iterator is still fail-fast: a traversal is many calls, and another thread can write between them. The page's fix is to hold the wrapper's own lock for the whole traversal:

Write `removeIf(List<String> syncList, Predicate<String> doomed)` in `SyncPurge`. `syncList` was made by `Collections.synchronizedList`, and other threads use it. Remove every element for which `doomed` is true, in place.

items: with `["a", "bb", "ccc"]` and `s -> s.length() > 1`, the list becomes `["a"]`;
**the lock is held for the whole traversal**: every time `doomed` is tested, the current thread holds the lock of `syncList` itself, the wrapper, not some other object;

do it the page's way, with one `synchronized (syncList)` block of your own around the whole job: every call your method makes on the list, from the first read to the last removal, runs inside that block. The wrapper's own per-call locking, `syncList.removeIf` included, does not count, and neither does a second pass or a rebuild after the block has ended.

cases.says: [a, bb, ccc] without the longer words is [a].
Each time doomed is tested, the current thread holds the synchronized list's own lock.
Every call the job makes on the list runs inside one synchronized (syncList) block of SyncPurge's own.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Collections.synchronizedList still hands out a fail-fast iterator, so a traversal holds the wrapper's own lock for its whole length.
